newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases, turnover up.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases, turnover up.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index eased 4.58 points to close at 3289.10 on Thursday but heavy foreign demand for selected shares increased turnover, bourse officials and brokers said.
Turnover was posted at 63.280 million shillings traded on 1,1190,833 shares from 37.675 million on 1,189,592 shares.
Foreign investors bought a total of 139,800 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at a reserve price of 96, unchanged, while 200,000 shares of Sasini Tea & Coffee at 80 from 76.
On the ordinary board closed at 90 from 96 on Wednesday and was a contributor to the index's downslide.
The bank has been fluctuating between 88 and 96 levels on mixed perceptions in the market.
"Foreigners are willing to pay an average six-shillings premium on the share but in big lots," a senior broker said.
On average, shares eased marginally, and brokers said the market would continue downwards as the market was slowing down.
"The market is rather stagnant now," a broker said, "and as a result interest is shifting from equities to the money market, albeit slowly."
Barclays bank eased to 99.50 from 100 while Kenya Breweries shed two shillings to close at 35. National Bank of Kenya closed at 15.50 from 15.95.
Kakuzi was unchanged at 101 while Kenya Airways edged to 8.10 from 8.

Bonds traded on the bourse are pegged to the 91-day treasury bill and offer competitive rates at 21 percent. The Central Bank of Kenya floating rate treasury bond traded 100,000 shillings at 101.6098 percent from 101.2000 percent.
